text: Freelancers get paid late. Buyers who pay strangers get burned. Proofhold ties a PayPal payment to a definition of done that both sides agree to.
The money is held by PayPal, never by Proofhold, and it only moves when the agreed proof arrives.
The seller writes the brief in plain words. Gemini compiles it into an acceptance test: the things a machine can measure, and the judgement calls it cannot.
The buyer gets one link, reads the same test, and approves a PayPal authorization. Not a payment. The test's hash is written into the PayPal order, so the agreement travels with the money.
The seller delivers. Validators measure the files. The examiner judges only what a machine cannot, and shows its reasons. If it is unsure, it abstains, and an abstention never releases money.
The buyer confirms, or the window closes. PayPal captures, and the seal is stamped.
Every hold lives in one ledger. An objection goes to review, and a dispute after capture goes to PayPal with the evidence already filed.
This take used the built-in PayPal simulator, so it could run unattended. The same flow has run against the PayPal sandbox: a real authorization, and a real capture.
Proofhold. Open source, and honest about what is real.
